"Create a 3D first-person \"Pokémon Snap Arena\" style game using Low-Poly Cel-Shaded (Toon Shading) graphics with bright, clean colors.
1. Environment: A closed circular arena with a dirt/sand floor and simplified stadium audience stands in the background.
2. Characters: Three Pokémon-style creatures (a fire monster, a water monster, and a grass monster) running and moving randomly around the arena.
3. Controls @COMMENT_BODY@ Camera: The player is static at the center of the arena, controlling a first-person camera that can rotate 360 degrees using the mouse or touch drag.
4. Core Mechanic (Photography):
Left click / tap triggers a camera shot (with a flash effect and shutter sound effect).
Scoring system:
+100 pts: Basic photo if the creature is anywhere in the frame.
+200 pts: If the creature is centered on the screen.
+300 pts: Bonus if captured during a special attack animation (each creature triggers a visual attack particle every 5 seconds).
5. User Interface (UI):
Display a \"Shots Remaining\" counter (starts at 15).
Display \"Total Score\" in the top-left corner.
Show a \"Game Over / Final Score\" summary screen when shots reach 0.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page

  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs

Storage:

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D first-person “Pokémon Snap Arena” style game with bright low-poly toon visuals, roaming elemental creatures, photo scoring, and a 15-shot game loop.

## Requirements
- Circular dirt/sand arena with simplified stadium audience stands.
- Three Pokémon-style creatures (fire, water, grass) move around randomly and have visual special attacks every 5 seconds.
- Player stays at arena center and rotates camera via mouse or touch drag.
- Click/tap takes a photo with flash and shutter sound.
- Score: +100 for a creature in frame, +200 if centered, +300 during a special attack.
- HUD shows total score and shots remaining; game-over summary at zero shots.
- Do not ask questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them upon completion.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone `index.html` using Three.js from jsDelivr, with original handmade creature shapes rather than third-party models.
- Added a start screen and keyboard camera movement/spacebar shooting in addition to requested pointer/touch controls.
- Set initial camera yaw to face Sprout so a creature is visible immediately.

## Work State

### Completed
- Built the arena scene, audience, creature models/animations, special attack effects, camera controls, photo scoring, synthesized shutter sound, HUD, start and game-over screens in `index.html`.
- Tested in Chromium via Playwright/SwiftShader; confirmed target detection, shooting, and a score of `0300` with shots decremented to `14`.
- Saved and inspected screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/snap-arena.jpg`.

### Active
- No active edits currently.

### Blocked
- Browser emitted a 404 for a resource during testing; source was not identified. Game itself rendered and basic gameplay worked.

## Next Move
1. Optionally investigate the 404 and run a broader gameplay/browser check, including shots reaching zero and restart.
2. Summarize implementation and assumptions briefly to the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Local test server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Playwright CLI could not find its bundled Chromium; verification succeeded using `/usr/bin/chromium` directly with Playwright and SwiftShader.

input.command: node -e "const {chromium}=require('/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/node_modules/playwright'); (async()=>{const b=await chromium.launch({executablePath:'/usr/bin/chromium',headless:true,args:['--no-sandbox','--use-gl=angle','--use-angle=swiftshader']});const p=await b.newPage({viewport:{width:1280,height:800}});let errors=[];p.on('pageerror',e=>errors.push(e.message));await p.goto('http://localhost:3002');await p.locator('#startButton').click();for(let i=0;i<15;i++){await p.mouse.click(640,400);await p.waitForTimeout(70)}await p.waitForTimeout(950);console.log(JSON.stringify({shots:await p.locator('#shots').innerText(),gameOver:await p.locator('#gameover').evaluate(e=>e.classList.contains('show')),final:await p.locator('#finalScore').innerText(),errors}));await p.locator('#restartButton').click();console.log(JSON.stringify({restartShots:await p.locator('#shots').innerText(),gameOverHidden:!(await p.locator('#gameover').evaluate(e=>e.classList.contains('show')))}));await b.close()})().catch(e=>{console.error(e);process.exit(1)})"

Implemented the playable game in `index.html`. It includes the arena, three original elemental creatures with roaming and special-attack animations, mouse/touch camera controls, photo scoring and shutter effects, a 15-shot HUD, and a game-over screen with restart.

Assumption: the creatures are original Pokémon-style designs rather than existing Pokémon. I verified shooting, reaching zero shots, the final score screen, and restart in Chromium.

Animations & Behavior:Idle Animation: Give each creature a distinct idle loop (e.g., Fire creature bouncing lightly on its feet, Grass creature twitching ears, Water creature swaying tail).
Attack/Pose Animation (Every 5s):
Fire: Rears back and breathes a brief 3D particle cone of fire into the air.
Water: Spins around and shoots a jet of blue water bubbles upwards.
Grass: Stomps the ground and summons sharp glowing green leaves that spin around it.
Expressive Reactions: When photographed, play a quick "spotted" animation (a tiny surprise star particle above its head and a cute jump).

Viewfinder Frame: Overlay a camera lens HUD with stylized corner brackets, a battery icon in the top right, and a red pulsing "REC" indicator.
Flash Effect: When taking a photo, display a brief bright white screen flash with a classic 8-bit or crisp mechanical shutter audio cue.
Score Popups: When a photo is taken, show floating combat-style text over the target showing "+100" (white text), "+200 CENTER!" (yellow text), or "+300 PERFECT ACTION!" (gold bold text with star particles).
